title: Logarithmic section algebra with at most one degree-zero component
statement: Let $T$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\pi:Y\to T$ a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] family with nonempty connected reduced nodal geometric fibres of pure dimension one [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres], of arithmetic genus $g\geq2$ (meaning $\dim_\Omega H^1(Y_\Omega,\mathcal O)=g$). Let $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ be disjoint sections in the relative smooth locus, $r\geq0$. Set $D=\sum_i a_i(T)$, an effective Cartier divisor, with invertible module $\mathcal O_Y(D)$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. The canonical relative dualizing invertible module $\omega_{Y/T}$ exists with the adjunction normalization [def-trf-nodal-dualizing-datum] and commutes with arbitrary base change. For $L=\omega_{Y/T}\otimes\mathcal O_Y(D)$ its degree on a normalized geometric component $V$ is $2g(V)-2+b_V+m_V$, where $b_V$ counts branches of nodes and $m_V$ counts markings; genus, normalization and degree use [def-pc-genus], [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. Assume all these degrees are nonnegative, and each geometric fibre has at most one component of degree zero; if present it is a smooth rational component with exactly two special points (branches of nodes or markings). For every $m\geq2$, $\pi_*L^{\otimes m}$ is finite locally free and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change. Evaluation of $L^{\otimes3}$ is surjective and the graded algebra $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{j\geq0}\pi_*L^{\otimes3j}$ is generated by its finite locally free degree-one part. With section multiplication and relative Proj [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures], [def-nagata-relative-proj], evaluation defines $q:Y\to X=\operatorname{Proj}_T\mathcal A$. The family $X\to T$ is flat and finitely presented and has a closed immersion into $\mathbf P_T(\pi_*L^{\otimes3})$, hence is projective in [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. Its geometric fibres are connected nodal curves of genus $g$; the sections $q a_i$ are disjoint and smooth and satisfy the stability inequalities of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve]. On geometric fibres $q$ contracts precisely the degree-zero component to a point and is an isomorphism away from it. If there is no degree-zero component in any geometric fibre, $q$ is an isomorphism. This construction, including $q$, commutes with arbitrary base change and with isomorphisms preserving each marking. It is unique up to unique isomorphism commuting with $q$ among maps from $Y$ to stable $r$-pointed families which, on every geometric fibre, are isomorphisms away from and contract exactly those degree-zero components; in the absence of such a component the fibre map is required to be an isomorphism.

source.place: Section 1, Theorem 1.8, Corollaries 1.9 and 1.11; Section 2, Proposition 2.1 (printed pp.172--175): degree-zero logarithmic components and their section-algebra contraction. Local PDF WANTED; primary-author scan consulted online.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proper-nodal-dualizing-base-change] to $\pi$. This gives the canonical relative dualizing invertible module with precisely the required fundamental-class normalization and arbitrary-base-change comparisons. Each marking is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion]. On the relative smooth locus its image is Cartier by [lem-trf-smooth-curve-section-cartier]; outside that closed image its ideal is the unit ideal, so the Cartier property holds on $Y$. Disjointness means locally at most one marked ideal is nontrivial, so their product defines the effective Cartier sum $D$; for $r=0$ it is the unit ideal. The sum is a disjoint union of copies of $T$, hence flat over $T$. The relative Cartier pullback theorem [lem-pc-recd-pullback] therefore identifies this divisor and its twist after every base change. Tensoring with the dualizing comparison identifies the pulled-back $L$ with the log dualizing line of the pulled-back marked family.

source.place: Tag 0E6R; smooth-section Cartier property Tag 067R; relative Cartier pullback Tag 062T.

proof.text: On a normalized geometric component $V$, the dualizing comparison in [lem-sfb-proper-nodal-dualizing-base-change] is $\Omega^1_V(B_V)$ and has degree $2g(V)-2+b_V$. A marking is at a smooth point, where normalization is an isomorphism, so its local Cartier parameter pulls back to one reduced rational point. There are $m_V$ such distinct points and none is a branch in $B_V$. The effective-divisor tensor-degree formula in [lem-pc-degree-base-change] adds $m_V$ to the degree. This gives $\deg L|_V=2g(V)-2+b_V+m_V$, including self-nodes, which contribute two branches, and the empty divisor.

source.place: Tag 0C4D normalization description and degree of an effective divisor; the dualizing degree is supplied by the cited arbitrary-base nodal lemma.

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed geometric fibre $C$. If it has a zero-degree component $E$, the hypotheses say it is smooth rational with two special points. It cannot be all of $C$, since its arithmetic genus would be zero instead of $g\geq2$. Its boundary with the reduced complement $C_0$ is therefore nonempty. The two possibilities are a tail with one attaching node and one marking, or a bridge with two attaching nodes and no marking. The nodal local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ shows that $C_0$ is nodal and smooth at each attachment and that $C_0\cap E$ is the reduced set of those one or two points. Apply [lem-trf-relative-nodal-point-pinching] to $C_0$, over the reference scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, identifying these boundary points to one point. Properness of $C_0$ follows from closed-immersion properness and composition in [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Pinching gives a proper nodal curve $C'$; a one-point pinch changes nothing locally, and a two-point pinch gives exactly a node, including when its two branches belong to one component. The maps $C_0\to C'$ and the constant map $E\to C'$ agree on the boundary. Since $C$ is reduced, it is the scheme-theoretic union $C_0\cup E$, so [lem-trf-closed-union-pushout] glues them to $c:C\to C'$. This map contracts exactly $E$ and is an isomorphism off it. It is surjective, so $C'$ is connected; it is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated]. If no $E$ exists set $C'=C$ and $c=1$.

source.place: Tags 0E3H (example-rational-tail), 0E3M (example-rational-bridge); pinching and closed-union facts used through their cited node statements.

proof.text: Give $C'$ the images of the old markings. In the tail case its unique marking on $E$ moves to the smooth attaching point of $C_0$, which was not an old marking; in the bridge case the contracted component has no marking and the new point is a node. Thus all markings remain distinct and smooth. The map $c$ satisfies every hypothesis of [lem-sfb-elementary-nodal-contraction-direct-image]. That node identifies $H^1(C',\mathcal O)$ with $H^1(C,\mathcal O)$ and $c^*\omega_{C'}(D')$ with $L_C$. The remaining components and their normalizations are unchanged. A tail replaces one nodal branch by one marking; a bridge replaces its two attaching branches by the branches of a new node. Thus on each remaining component $b_V+m_V$ and its genus are unchanged. All of its log degrees are positive, since there was at most one zero component. $C'$ is connected as the image of connected $C$ and has genus $g$. Its positive degrees imply the required stability inequalities directly: genus zero needs at least three special points and genus one at least one.

source.place: Section 1, Lemma 1.6, applied to the explicitly constructed tail or bridge quotient; component count after contraction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stable-pointed-field-linear-series] to the proper nodal pointed $C'$ of step 4. For $m\geq2$ its logarithmic $m$th power has no positive cohomology and is globally generated. For $m=3$ it is very ample and normally generated. The cohomology and multiplication comparisons of [lem-sfb-elementary-nodal-contraction-direct-image] identify its sections and cohomology with those of $L_C^{\otimes m}$. Pulling back its surjective evaluation by $c$ therefore proves global generation on $C$. The complete cubic evaluation of $C$ is exactly $c$ followed by the closed embedding of $C'$. Its section ring is the full cubic section ring of $C'$ and is generated in degree one. The same contraction lemma gives $c_*\mathcal O_C=\mathcal O_{C'}$ and zero positive direct images, and the closed embedding is affine, so [lem-sc-affine-derived-pushforward-t-exact] shows that the evaluation map into projective space has structure-sheaf direct image $\mathcal O_{C'}$ and zero positive direct images.

source.place: Theorem 1.8, Corollary 1.9, and Lemma 1.6; their separate roles are field linear series and cohomology of a supplied contraction.

proof.text: For each $m\geq2$, the module $L^{\otimes m}$ is finitely presented and flat over $T$, since it is invertible on a flat $T$-scheme. By [lem-pc-rf-perfect-base-change], $K_m=R\pi_*L^{\otimes m}$ is perfect and its canonical derived base-change map is an isomorphism for every base change. Step 5 says each geometric derived fibre is concentrated in degree zero. Use [def-pc-perfect-complex] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] to choose bounded finite-free representatives locally before applying the current perfect-locus statement. For a point $t$, let $r_t$ be the dimension of that fibre. The rank-$r_t$, degree-zero open of [lem-pc-perfect-locus] contains $t$: a finite-dimensional field complex concentrated in degree zero is that vector space in degree zero. These opens cover $T$. On each, $K_m$ is a finite locally free module in degree zero; these modules agree on overlaps as $H^0(K_m)$. Hence $\pi_*L^{\otimes m}$ is finite locally free. Its derived pullback is ordinary pullback, so the canonical derived comparison gives exactly arbitrary base change for this direct image. No reduced or Noetherian base is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0A1H and 0B91 (perfect direct image and canonical base change); Tag 0B9S degree-zero locus, used through the existing perfect-locus node.

proof.text: Put $M=L^{\otimes3}$ and $A_j=\pi_*M^{\otimes j}$. By [lem-sc-proper-flat-global-sections], $A_0=\mathcal O_T$ universally, because $\pi$ is proper flat finitely presented with reduced connected geometric fibres. All $A_j$ for $j>0$ are finite locally free and satisfy arbitrary base change by step 6. On a stalk of $Y$, the cokernel of $\pi^*A_1\to M$ is finite. Its residue at that point vanishes by fibrewise global generation in step 5 and the canonical section base-change comparison. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] with the empty generating set to this cokernel proves evaluation is surjective. For each $j$, the same argument on stalks of $T$ applies to the finite cokernel of $\operatorname{Sym}^j A_1\to A_j$; its residue vanishes by normal generation in step 5. These maps are therefore surjective for every $j$, which is precisely generation of $\mathcal A$ by its degree-one part.

source.place: Tag 0E0L universal structure pushforward; Nakayama Tag 00DV; Knudsen Proposition 2.1, relative evaluation and generation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-section-image-flat-fp] to $\pi$ and $M$. Step 5 supplies fibrewise acyclicity for every positive power of $M$ and the asserted scheme-theoretic fibre image with its cohomologically trivial map; steps 6--7 supply universal positive-degree base change, finite local freeness, evaluation and multiplication. Thus $X=\operatorname{Proj}_T\mathcal A$ is flat and finitely presented, and has the required closed immersion into $\mathbf P_T(A_1)$. Evaluation defines a proper surjection $q:Y\to X$. On each geometric fibre the image comparison identifies it with the explicitly constructed $c:C\to C'$ of steps 3--5, not merely with a set-theoretic image. It follows that the fibres of $X$ are connected nodal curves of genus $g$, and $q$ contracts precisely the zero-degree component and is an isomorphism elsewhere. The images of distinct markings remain distinct on every geometric fibre, so their images in $X$ are disjoint. They lie in the relative smooth locus by [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion], since $X/T$ is flat and finitely presented and their fibre points are smooth. Their component stability was checked in step 4; this is exactly [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve].

source.place: Proposition 2.1, relative Proj construction; the finite-presentation passage is isolated in the cited relative-image lemma; fibre identification uses the explicit previous quotient.

proof.text: If every geometric fibre has positive degrees, the description in step 8 says $q$ is a fibrewise isomorphism. Apply [lem-sfb-universal-isomorphism-open] with base $T$, source $Y$, target $X$ and map $q$. The target is proper by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper]. The source is proper, flat and finitely presented; the target is proper and finitely presented by its projective-bundle embedding. The isomorphism open contains every geometric point and therefore every point of $T$, so equals $T$. Consequently $q$ itself is an isomorphism, including over a nonreduced base.

source.place: Tag 05XD, universal-isomorphism open, with all structural hypotheses supplied in steps 1 and 8.

proof.text: For an arbitrary $u:T'\to T$, the canonical comparisons in steps 1 and 6--7 give a graded algebra isomorphism $u^*\mathcal A\simeq\bigoplus_j\pi'_*L'^{\otimes3j}$. It respects multiplication because section pullback sends a tensor product of two sections to the tensor product of their pullbacks. Apply [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] to identify $X\times_TT'$ with the Proj of this pulled-back algebra. Under that identification the two evaluation maps agree: on each standard chart they both send a homogeneous fraction $a/s^n$ to the evaluated ratio $a/s^n$ on $Y'$. The same check for an isomorphism of families preserving each marking identifies the canonical dualizing lines, divisor twists, section algebras and evaluation maps. Composition is respected on sections and on homogeneous fractions, proving the requested functoriality including $q$.

Let $p:Y\to Z$ be another map of $r$-pointed families to a stable labelled $r$-pointed family $(Z,b_1,\ldots,b_r)$, so $pa_i=b_i$ for every $i$ (this is the hypothesis $ca_i=b_i$ of the contraction lemma below; without it uniqueness fails, e.g. for $Z=X$ with permuted labels and $p=q$), satisfying the prescribed fibre contractions. The stable target $Z/T$ is proper by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper]. The map $p$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated], since $Y/T$ is proper and $Z/T$ is separated. Step 3 shows that each exceptional fibre component has exactly the tail/bridge type required by [lem-sfb-elementary-nodal-contraction-direct-image]. That lemma, now applied to the supplied $p$, gives a canonical, multiplication-preserving isomorphism $\bigoplus_j(Z\to T)_*\omega_{Z/T}(D_Z)^{\otimes3j}\simeq\mathcal A$. Apply [lem-sfb-stable-pointed-field-linear-series] on the fibres of $Z$ and then repeat the degree-zero perfect-locus argument of step 6 and the Nakayama argument of step 7 for $Z$. The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-relative-section-image-flat-fp] hold for its log cubic: its fibre evaluation is a closed immersion, so its structure-image condition holds, and [lem-sc-affine-derived-pushforward-t-exact] gives the positive-direct-image vanishing. Its evaluation map $Z\to\operatorname{Proj}_T\mathcal A=X$ is fibrewise an isomorphism. By [lem-sfb-universal-isomorphism-open] it is an isomorphism $f:Z\xrightarrow{\sim}X$. The section-algebra comparison makes its evaluation quotient pull back to that of $Y$, so $fp=q$, and it preserves every label because $fb_i=fpa_i=qa_i$.

source.place: Proposition 2.1, uniqueness via Lemma 1.6 and canonical section algebras; relative isomorphism test Tag 05XD. The argument uses the supplied competing map, not the forgetful-moduli theorem.

proof.text: There is at most one such $f$. Indeed the contraction comparison in [lem-sfb-elementary-nodal-contraction-direct-image] gives $p_*\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_Z$, and $p$ is proper and surjective, hence a quotient map on underlying spaces. If $f_1p=f_2p=q$, surjectivity gives $|f_1|=|f_2|$. For any open $U\subset X$, their common inverse image $V\subset Z$ has $\mathcal O_Z(V)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_Y(p^{-1}V)$. The ring homomorphisms on $U$ for $f_1,f_2$ have the same composite with this injective homomorphism, so they agree. Thus their sheaf morphisms and underlying maps agree, giving $f_1=f_2$. This proves uniqueness commuting with $q$; the same reasoning applies after any base change.

source.place: Proposition 2.1, uniqueness; explicit ringed-space argument from the structure-pushforward isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Section 1 and Proposition 2.1, generalized from deletion of a distinguished marking to a proper nodal family with the stated single zero-component condition; local primary PDF unavailable. Stacks tools and all extra relative-image input are cited separately.
